links.description: The « Ouvrir PlanAstro » button of the message. Its origin is the public address of the service (`webUrl`); its path is always `/auth/link`; everything else is in the fragment, which a browser never sends to the service. On a phone where the application is installed, the operating system hands the whole address to the application (universal link on iOS, verified App Link on Android, both declared for the path `/auth/link`); the application uses it only when it has a request in progress on this device, for the address the person typed: it reads `token` and calls POST /v1/sign-in/verify with `linkToken` and that address; otherwise it ignores the token and opens its sign-in screen. Anywhere else the browser opens the page below, which shows the code and nothing else.

exchanges.description: Any visit of the link in a browser — a person on a computer, or a mail scanner. The service receives no token and no code (they are in the fragment); it answers the same static page every time, reads nothing, writes nothing, uses up nothing and opens no session. The page reads the fragment in the browser and shows « Votre code de connexion », the code in large digits and « Valable encore 8 minutes » (or « Ce code a expiré » past `expires`). A fragment it cannot read shows only a sentence asking to use the code of the message.
A private server signing in by password sends no message and has no such page.
